questions.question_text:
A container holds $V=4t^{2}+7t$ litres of water after $t$ minutes.
Find the rate at which the volume is increasing when $t=3$ minutes.

options.why: Differentiated $4t^{2}$ correctly but dropped the derivative of the $7t$ term.
Differentiated $4t^{2}$ as $4t$, halving the coefficient, then added $7$.
Differentiated $4t^{2}$ as $4t$ and also dropped the derivative of $7t$.

questions.question_text:
A patient's weight $W$ kilograms after $t$ weeks satisfies $\dfrac{dW}{dt}=-3.5$ at $t=8$ weeks.
Which statement describes the weight at $t=8$ weeks?

options.text: It is decreasing at $3.5$ kg per week.
It is increasing at $3.5$ kg per week.
options.why: Ignored the negative sign and read a falling quantity as a rising one.

options.text: It is decreasing at $-3.5$ kg per week.
options.why: Reported a decrease of a negative amount, double-counting the negative sign.

options.text: It is increasing at $-3.5$ kg per week.
options.why: Kept the sign in the amount but stated the wrong direction as well.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dW}{dt}=-3.5$
The rate is negative, so the weight is falling.
The size of the rate is $3.5$, so the weight is decreasing at $3.5$ kilograms per week.

questions.question_text:
A stone is thrown upward so that its height is $h=2+24t-4t^{2}$ metres after $t$ seconds.
Find the time at which the height is momentarily not changing.

options.why: Included the constant $2$ in the derivative, solving $26-8t=0$.
Differentiated $-4t^{2}$ as $-4t$, solving $24-4t=0$.
Both kept the constant $2$ and differentiated $-4t^{2}$ as $-4t$, solving $26-4t=0$.

questions.question_text:
A quantity of liquid is $Q=t^{3}-4t^{2}+9t$ litres after $t$ hours.
Find $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}$ when $t=5$ hours.

options.why: Differentiated twice but dropped the $-8t$ term when differentiating $-4t^{2}$ the second time.
Differentiated $3t^{2}$ as $3t$ instead of $6t$ at the second stage.
Differentiated $3t^{2}$ as $3t$ and also lost the $-8$ from the second term.

questions.question_text:
The number of insects in a colony is $N=300+24t-t^{2}$ after $t$ weeks.
At $t=10$ weeks, is $N$ increasing or decreasing, and at what rate?

options.why: Computed the rate correctly as $+4$ but read the positive sign as a decrease.
Differentiated $-t^{2}$ as $+2t$, giving $24+2t$ instead of $24-2t$.
Differentiated $-t^{2}$ as $+2t$ and also stated the wrong direction.

questions.solution_text:
$N=300+24t-t^{2}$
$\dfrac{dN}{dt}=24-2t$
$\text{At }t=10:$
$\dfrac{dN}{dt}=24-2(10)$
$=4\text{ insects/week}$
The rate is positive, so the colony is increasing at $4$ insects per week.

questions.question_text:
A pool fills so that $V=2t^{2}+9t$ kilolitres after $t$ minutes.
Find the time at which the water is flowing in at $45$ kilolitres per minute.

options.why: Differentiated correctly but solved $4t=45$, forgetting to subtract the $9$ first.
Differentiated $2t^{2}$ as $2t$, then solved $2t+9=45$.
Differentiated $2t^{2}$ as $2t$ and also forgot to subtract the $9$, solving $2t=45$.

questions.question_text:
For the volume $V$ of water in a tank, $\dfrac{dV}{dt}<0$ and $\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}>0$ at $t=5$ hours.
Which statement is true at that time?

options.text: The volume is falling, and the rate of fall is slowing down.
The volume is falling, and the rate of fall is speeding up.
options.why: Read a positive second derivative as making a negative rate more negative.

options.text: The volume is rising, and the rate of rise is slowing down.
options.why: Took the sign of the second derivative as the direction of the volume.

options.text: The volume is rising, and the rate of rise is speeding up.
options.why: Used the positive second derivative for both the direction and the trend, ignoring $\dfrac{dV}{dt}<0$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}<0$, so the volume is decreasing.
$\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}>0$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ is increasing towards zero.
A negative rate moving towards zero is a fall that is slowing down.

questions.question_text:
A liquid cools so that $T=15+48e^{-0.25t}$ degrees Celsius after $t$ minutes.
Find $\dfrac{dT}{dt}$ when $t=8$ minutes, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Lost the negative sign from the index when applying the chain rule.
Differentiated $e^{-0.25t}$ as $e^{-0.25t}$, omitting the factor $-0.25$, then attached a negative sign.
Omitted the factor $-0.25$ from the chain rule and also lost the negative sign.
